intro: This last unit looks back and then looks forward. First it looks at Michael Heiser's legacy: where he worked, how he taught, and how his ideas about the divine council, the Watchers and the gods of the nations spread through books, a long-running podcast and popular teaching. It also looks at what happened when other people used his name, sometimes carefully and sometimes for claims he rejected, such as ancient astronauts or giants building the pyramids.

Then the unit turns to you. In the capstone you choose one hard question from this course, gather the primary texts from the Hebrew Bible, 1 Enoch and the New Testament, and state Heiser's reading beside at least one other. You weigh the evidence and write a fair argument. You cite every text by book, chapter, verse and translation, and you present it calmly to classmates who may believe differently.

By the end you will be able to check a claim against the text and against a scholar's own words, and to explain a disputed passage fairly. You will also be able to disagree with respect. These skills reach well beyond this course. They help with any text, any scholar and any viral video.
bigQuestion: How do we test claims about ancient texts, and argue fairly about them with readers who see them differently?

timeline.t: The King James Version is published, a public-domain translation still quoted today
R. H. Charles publishes his English translation of the Book of Enoch
The first Dead Sea Scrolls are found near the Dead Sea
Zecharia Sitchin publishes The 12th Planet, an ancient-astronaut book Heiser later answered
Heiser completes his PhD dissertation on the divine council at the University of Wisconsin–Madison
Heiser begins the Naked Bible Podcast
Lexham Press publishes The Unseen Realm and Supernatural
Demons and A Companion to the Book of Enoch appear
Heiser dies in February; the Naked Bible Podcast comes to an end

test.q: What was Heiser's role at Logos Bible Software?
test.why: Heiser served as scholar-in-residence at Logos, later called Faithlife.

test.q: When did the Naked Bible Podcast run?
test.why: The podcast began in 2014 and ended in 2023, the year Heiser died.

test.q: What did Heiser argue about Sitchin's reading of the Anunnaki?
choices: The tablets show them as gods, not space travelers
They are the same as the Nephilim
The tablets prove they came from Nibiru
test.why: Heiser argued the Mesopotamian texts present the Anunnaki as gods and do not describe space travel.

test.q: Where did Heiser think the word Nephilim most likely came from?
test.why: Heiser argued for an Aramaic origin meaning giant, which fits the Septuagint's gigantes.

test.q: Which fact best answers the claim that the Bible says giants built the pyramids?
choices: Genesis never mentions pyramids, and its giant stories are set in Canaan
The KJV uses the word giants
test.why: The Bible does not link giants with the pyramids; Numbers and Deuteronomy place them in and near Canaan.

test.q: Which witness reads sons of God in Deuteronomy 32:8?
test.why: 4QDeut-j reads sons of God; the Masoretic Text and the KJV read sons (children) of Israel.

test.q: Which reading of the sons of God did Augustine teach?
test.why: Augustine, in The City of God, taught the Sethite view.

test.q: Which statement about Jude 14–15 is accurate?
test.why: Jude presents a prophecy of Enoch that closely matches 1 Enoch 1:9.

test.q: In Reversing Hermon (2017), what did Heiser argue about Jesus' mission?
choices: It began at the tower of Babel
It had no link to the Old Testament
It reverses the Watchers' rebellion linked with Mount Hermon
test.why: Heiser argued the Gospels echo Hermon to show Jesus reversing the rebellion 1 Enoch places there.

test.q: Which is a primary source for a paper on 1 Peter 3:19?
test.why: The passage itself is the primary source; everything written about it is secondary.

choices: In The Unseen Realm (2015), Heiser argued that the elohim of Psalm 82 are heavenly beings
Heiser taught that 1 Enoch is in every Bible
Heiser proved giants built the pyramids
Heiser said aliens are the Anunnaki
test.why: It reports a view Heiser actually held, with the book and year.

choices: The strongest case against your thesis, stated and answered fairly
test.why: A strong paper states the best case against its thesis and answers it fairly.

test.q: Which translation may be quoted word for word in this course?
choices: Heiser's own translation in a 2015 book
test.why: The KJV is in the public domain. Modern translations and Heiser's books are under copyright.

test.q: What does weighing the evidence decide in a capstone?
choices: Which reading best explains a text
test.why: Weighing judges which reading best explains the text, not what anyone should believe.

test.q: A classmate disagrees during your presentation. What is the best response?
choices: Thank them and ask which text or witness they would weigh differently
test.why: Turning to the evidence keeps the disagreement calm, respectful and useful.

write.prompt: Choose one question: Who are the sons of God in Genesis 6? Is 1 Peter 3:19 about the Watchers? Cite two or three passages (for example Genesis 6:1–4, 1 Enoch 6:1–6, Jude 14–15, 2 Peter 2:4). Explain what each text says, how Heiser read it, and how at least one other reader has read it. Then weigh the readings.
tips: Name every text by book, chapter, verse and translation, such as Genesis 6:4, King James Version (1611).
Attribute every view: Heiser argues, Augustine read, Jewish tradition records.
State each reading at its strongest before you weigh it.
Paraphrase Heiser in your own words and give the book and year; never quote his books.
Let your conclusion be as firm as the evidence, and no firmer.
